name: Question 4
problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $E(4,-2,5)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨11,0,5⟩+s⟨7,-3,4⟩$ and $r=⟨12,-2,4⟩+t⟨3,-5,1⟩.$
worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨7,-3,4⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨3,-5,1⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $E(4,-2,5)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $e=⟨4,-2,5⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =e+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨4,-2,5⟩+s⟨7,-3,4⟩+t⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point E(4,−2,5) and is parallel to the lines r=⟨11,0,5⟩+s⟨7,−3,4⟩ and r=⟨12,−2,4⟩+t⟨3,−5,1⟩.

a
r=⟨4,−2,5⟩+s⟨7,−4,3⟩+t⟨1,−5,3⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨5,−2,4⟩+s⟨7,3,4⟩+t⟨3,5,2⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨4,−2,5⟩+s⟨4,−3,7⟩+t⟨1,−5,3⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨4,−5,2⟩+s⟨−3,−7,4⟩+t⟨3,5,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨4,−2,5⟩+s⟨7,−3,4⟩+t⟨3,−5,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The direction vectors of the lines are v1=⟨7,−3,4⟩ and v2=⟨3,−5,1⟩, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point E(4,−2,5) lies on the plane and its position vector is e=⟨4,−2,5⟩.

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

r=e+sv1+tv2r=⟨4,−2,5⟩+s⟨7,−3,4⟩+t⟨3,−5,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞).
